newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian radar deal close to agreement - govt.
newsitem.headline: Australian radar deal close to agreement - govt.

text.p: Australian state telecoms giant Telstra Corp was close to finalising the handover of a troubled A$1.1 billion radar project to Lockheed Martin Corp and the unlisted Transfield Defence System, the government said on Sunday.
Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said he had pressed the companies to resolve outstanding issues, including a payment from Telstra to the new managers, and expected agreement within weeks.
"No doubt, that will be sorted out in the next few weeks. As I understand it, it's pretty close," he said in a television interview.
Lockheed and Transfield announced a joint venture in February to take over the troubled Jindalee Operational Network (JORN) project, which is running over-budget and years behind schedule.
McLachlan said that since February, the companies had been looking at how much it would cost to complete the project.
"I don't think it's any secret that there will be some payment from Telstra to Lockheed," he said.
The cost to the Australian government has already been capped at A$1.1 billion, so any over-run must be sorted out between Telstra and the new project managers.
McLachlan said he did not expect the issue to affect the government's planned sale of one-third of Telstra later this year.
"As long as the matter's sorted out ... the amounts sorted out, then it won't ... affect the float at all," he said.
The government hopes to raise at least A$8 billion from the partial privatisation.
